intro: Some parts of the Talmud read like a law book. Others read like a book of stories and advice. This unit shows that the two belong together. You will read the opening chapters of Pirkei Avot, the Chapters of the Fathers, and parts of two tractates, Ta'anit and Yoma.

Avot begins with a chain of teachers and a set of short sayings: judge slowly, pursue peace, and do not stop the work even if you cannot finish it. Ta'anit tells of fasts for rain and of Honi, who drew a circle and would not leave it. Yoma rules that saving a life comes before Shabbat, and that a holy day cannot clear a wrong done to another person.

By the end, you will be able to cite these passages by tractate and page, explain the argument behind a ruling, and describe how different Jewish readers have understood them. Keep asking two questions of every text: how does the argument move, and whom does the ruling protect?
bigQuestion: How do the Talmud's laws and stories work together to teach what a person owes to God, to others and to the future?

timeline.t: The first of the five pairs (zugot) teach, as rabbinic tradition dates them
Honi the circle-drawer (Onias in Josephus) is remembered for prayers for rain
Hillel and Shammai, the last pair, lead the sages
Rome destroys the Second Temple in Jerusalem
Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah teach
Judah the Prince edits the Mishnah, including Avot, Ta'anit and Yoma
Shmuel teaches in Babylonia: "live by them"
The Babylonian Talmud takes shape, with Gemara on Ta'anit and Yoma
Maimonides completes his law code, the Mishneh Torah
Charles Taylor publishes Sayings of the Jewish Fathers in Cambridge
The Jewish Publication Society publishes its English Tanakh

words.d: Chapters of the Fathers; a Mishnah tractate of ethical sayings
the first written collection of rabbinic law, edited around 200 CE
the discussion of the Mishnah that makes up most of the Talmud
the five pairs of teachers in Avot chapter 1
a rabbinic rule that keeps a person away from breaking a bigger law
turning or repentance; changing one's ways
the story and teaching parts of the Talmud
Jewish law as the rabbis develop it
saving a life; it comes before almost every other command
a unit of Talmudic discussion on one question

test.q: Who received the Torah from Moses, according to Avot 1:1?
test.why: Avot 1:1: Moses handed it to Joshua.

test.q: What does "make a fence around the Torah" mean?
choices: Build a wall around the Temple
Write the Torah on a wall
Add rules that keep people far from breaking a bigger law
test.why: A fence is a protective rabbinic rule.

test.q: Which list comes from Simeon the Just?
choices: Torah, worship and acts of loving-kindness
test.why: Avot 1:2 gives Simeon the Just's three pillars.

test.q: "If I am not for myself, who is for me?" is from which source?
test.why: Hillel asks the three questions in Avot 1:14.

choices: Do not judge until you reach his place
Receive every person with a cheerful face

test.q: What is the main idea of Rabbi Tarfon's saying?
choices: Work is less important than rest
You need not finish the work, but you may not stop
test.why: Avot 2 records Tarfon's balance of duty and limit.

test.q: What does Ta'anit mean, and what is it about?
choices: Fast; public fasts, mostly for rain

test.q: What did Honi do when the first rain was only a few drops?
choices: He said that was not what he asked for
test.why: Mishnah Ta'anit 3:8 shows Honi rejecting the drops.

test.q: What kind of text is the story of Honi's seventy-year sleep?
test.why: It is a story in the Gemara, Ta'anit 23a.

choices: Yom Kippur atones for all wrongs
Honi was placed under a ban
Rubble is cleared on Shabbat even when it is unclear if someone is alive
test.why: Yoma 8:7 applies pikuach nefesh even in doubt.

test.q: In Yoma 85a–b, what did the sages disagree about?
choices: Which verse proves that saving a life overrides Shabbat
Whether a life should be saved
test.why: All agreed on the rule; they argued about the proof.

test.q: What does "live by them" mean in the rabbis' reading of Leviticus 18:5?
choices: Live only in the land of Israel
Live by the laws, and not die by them

test.q: According to Mishnah Yoma 8:9, what can Yom Kippur NOT do by itself?
choices: Clear a wrong done before God
Clear a wrong done to another person
test.why: Wrongs between people need reconciliation first.

test.q: Which translation of Avot is public domain and from 1877?
choices: Charles Taylor's Sayings of the Jewish Fathers
test.why: Taylor's 1877 work is in the public domain.

test.q: Which pair of statements is attributed correctly?
choices: Rava: either companionship or death; Hillel: if not now, when?
Hillel: the day is short; Tarfon: if not now, when?
Shammai: live by them; Shmuel: cheerful face
Honi: judge favorably; Rava: fence around the Torah
test.why: Rava comments in Ta'anit 23a; Hillel speaks in Avot 1:14.

write.prompt: Do the Talmud's texts put people before rules? Cite two or three passages from this unit, such as Avot 2:4, Mishnah Ta'anit 2:1, Yoma 85b or Mishnah Yoma 8:9. Explain what each says and how different Jewish readers have understood it.
tips: Name each text by tractate and chapter or page.
Attribute every belief: "the Mishnah says," "Shmuel argues," "Reform readers often stress."
Show the argument's moves: question, proof, objection, answer.
Compare readings instead of judging which is true.
Use at least three terms from the unit, such as pikuach nefesh or teshuvah.
